r-surface.$description:
A product card is a thing you want to touch, so its corner is softer than a panel
you want to read. One step up the scale rather than an invented number, which is the rule an
extension holds to everywhere: it re-values a role, and the value it moves to is still Arena's.

r-surface-floating.$description:
The floating tier moves with the surface tier and stays one step below it, so a menu
still reads as lighter than the card it opens over. Moving one without the other is the
half-applied look the two roles exist to prevent.

r-control.$description:
A softer button. Not a pill: a pill reads as a tag or a filter chip, and a call to
action that looks like a filter is a call to action nobody presses.

r-control-sm.$description:
A checkbox box and a segment move with the buttons, one step below them, which is
the relationship roles.json authored and not a second decision taken here. Left behind, a 4px
checkbox beside a 10px button reads as a control the extension forgot rather than as a small
one, and it is the same half-applied look r-surface-floating exists to prevent one tier up.

r-field.$description:
Fields follow controls, because a form reads as one object when its inputs and its
submit button share a corner.

r-marker.$description:
A price badge sits on a rounder card, so a square-cornered marker would read as
stuck on rather than part of it.

bw-surface.$description:
The change this extension is actually about. Arena groups by drawing the region,
which is cheap in pixels and right for dense data; here the grouping is carried by elevation
and air instead, which is the Gestalt trade between common region and figure/ground.

Safe to remove because a surface is not a user interface component: WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of a
CONTROL's boundary and of a meaningful graphic, and a card is neither. bw-control and bw-field
are therefore untouched below, and bw-separator with them, because a table that lost the rules
between its rows when its frame went would stop being readable.

shadow-surface-rest.$description:
What replaces the border. The lightest step of the elevation scale, because a page
of product cards each carrying a dialog's depth reads as a pile rather than a grid.

It does most of its work in light. A warm-black shadow on a warm-black page is barely a boundary,
so in dark the base-100 to base-200 step is what still separates a card from the page and this
only deepens it. Verified by looking at intro/guidelines/design-extension.html in both themes,
which is the only way that could have been found.

shadow-control-raised.$description:
A call to action that lifts further than anything else on the page. This is where
an expressive extension spends most of its emphasis, and it is spent on one element per view,
which is the same rule as one primary accent per view.

lift-control.$description:
Two pixels, and no more: the travel has to read as an answer to the pointer rather
than as the layout moving. It is a length rather than an alias because the base value is 0 and
there is no scale step for a distance a control travels.

dur-hover.$description:
Slower than Arena's default, which is the whole difference between an interface
that acknowledges a pointer and one that responds to it. Still inside the transition range, so
nothing here becomes motion a person waits on.

fs-h1.$description:
A page heading that carries a page rather than titling a panel. The base ladder
accelerates gently because a console has many peers on screen at once; a landing has few, so the
jump from the body it sits over is wider here.

The reading sizes below h2 do not move, in this extension or in any other. Body and chrome text
is the one thing every voice shares, because how large a paragraph is set is a legibility
decision and not an expressive one. An extension widens the hierarchy by raising what shouts,
never by shrinking what is read.

fs-display.$description:
The step a hero headline is set at. 80 over 64 is a fifth again, which reads as a
different kind of page rather than as the same page with bigger type.

fs-hero.$description:
The largest step anything is actually set at, and the reason fs-hero was kept when
it had no consumer.
